output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server to new hardware, not from agency nurses. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone only. The warning was logged but the import reported success. Phone notifications per nurse in Pods A-C doubled (about 38 to 82 per shift). Acknowledgement times roughly doubled. Incidents rose about fourfold for core, agency and new-graduate nurses alike. Pod D still uses the old server and showed no change. Bedside alarm volume was flat, which argues against acuity and the monitor software update. Wireless coverage is unlikely to be the cause. Sick leave rose across the hospital, so the link between phone alarm load and sick leave is unproven. Capping agency use and reviewing named nurses would target the wrong cause and punish the wrong people. Switching off SpO2 and technical phone forwarding would remove protection while the central station is unstaffed at night. Next step: restore the old rule set (about 4 hours plus clinical validation) with Clinical Engineering and the alarm committee. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Pause the proposed reviews. Keep the agency question open for separate review.
